newsitem.title: CHINA: China banks trade 7.8b yuan debt in first month.
newsitem.headline: China banks trade 7.8b yuan debt in first month.

text.p: China's state banks traded 7.791 billion yuan in state debt contracts in the first month after interbank state debt trading began on June 16, the China Securities News said on Wednesday.

China's central bank, the People's Bank, in early June ordered the banks to stop trading state debt on the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges and regional debt trading centres, and to move their trading to the local currency interbank market.
By July 15, daily turnover in the 22 trading days had hit an average of 350 million yuan, the newspaper said.
"Trading has been dull," the newspaper said, mainly because of the time it was taking for the banks to move their positions to the new depository.
Problems had also arisen because of the low level of outstanding state debt to be traded, it said, adding that banks were unfamiliar with the new trading system.

China set up the Beijing-based depository, the China Government Securities Depository Trust and Clearing Co, in Feburary to coordinate all debt trading and to hold, clear and settle all state debt transactions.
Beijing has ordered all financial institutions to gradually move their state debt positions, previously deposited on the exchanges and local trading centres, to the central depository.
Industry sources said state banks had moved all their state debt positions to the depository and other financial institutions were expected to move the positions by the end of this year.
